title: AES standard on interconnections — Grounding and EMC practices — Shields of 25-way D-type connectors in balanced circuits
working_group: SC-05-05 (Working Group on Grounding and EMC Practices)
source_file: .env/AES-X249 AES standard on interconnections - Grounding and EMC practices - Shields of  25-way D-type connectors in balanced circuits/ReadyToMerge_With_AES48 _Project_X249_Shields_of_D-type_connectors_20240930.docx
abstract: Defines specific mechanical and electrical bonding requirements for 25-way D-subminiature (AES59 DB25) connectors to equipment shielding enclosures (chassis) to eliminate the Pin 1 problem in high-density multi-channel audio equipment.

key_elements.Csf: Contact Shroud Flange: The trapezoidal metal flange surrounding connector pins, installed inside enclosure pushing outward, providing direct metal-to-metal contact with the metallic chassis perimeter.
key_elements.Cjs: Contact Jack Screw: Hexagonal metal standoffs with 4-40 threaded holes that mechanically fasten connector and provide electrical bonding directly to the chassis shield plane.
key_elements.Dsc: Designated Shield Contacts: Pins 2, 5, 8, 11, 16, 19, 22, 25 in DB25 connector.
key_elements.So: Shield Overall: External cable outer braid.
key_elements.pin_13_prohibition: Under AES59, Pin 13 is unused. AES-X249 strictly prohibits bonding Shield Overall or any ground wire to Pin 13.

pcb_layout_rules.shield_plane: A dedicated PCB shield plane must route designated shield contacts directly to jackscrews and shroud flange.
pcb_layout_rules.segregation: Shield plane currents MUST be completely segregated from the internal audio signal circuit reference ground plane.
pcb_layout_rules.paint_warning: No non-conductive paint, anodization, or powder coat between shroud flange, jack screws, and metallic chassis.

relevance_to_balanced_audio: Extends AES48 chassis-grounding discipline to multi-channel DB25 connectors, solving RF and hum intrusion in compact high-channel-count converters.
